sections.title: Identification and habit
sections.text: The catalogue entry Cornus refers here to Cornus sanguinea, common dogwood, rather than the whole genus. This shrub or small tree of Europe and western Asia often reaches 3–4 m. Young twigs can be red, and the opposite leaves turn reddish in autumn.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Small white flowers are grouped in flat-topped clusters and develop into black fruits. The plate matches the twigs, leaves, and flower and fruit clusters. It differs from Cornus mas, with its white flowers and black fruits rather than early yellow flowers and elongated red fruits.
